problem: Long-horizon robot memory systems either rely on caption-only video memory (ReMEmbR), which becomes redundant on revisits and loses fine detail, or on object-centric static scene graphs, which collapse top-k retrieval into one local region. Task-driven graphs such as Clio need a predefined task list and re-aggregate all primitives whenever tasks change.
motivation: Robots deployed for hours or days must answer open-ended spatial, temporal and descriptive queries, often among many visually similar objects such as warehouse boxes. Feeding the full memory to an MLLM is too costly and induces hallucination, so a compact, non-redundant, task-relevant evidence set is needed that scales with memory length.
key_idea: Build a task-agnostic multimodal memory (captions + 3D primitives + keyframes), then at query time use captions to induce a small primitive subset, run Information Bottleneck clustering on it, and pick one representative caption per cluster as non-redundant evidence for an agentic MLLM.
insight: Deduplicating retrieval by task-conditioned IB clusters, rather than taking the top-k cosine hits, avoids redundant captions around one location, which is the failure mode of ReMEmbR in the qualitative examples. Running IB only on the caption-induced primitive subset keeps query time stable (about 30 s average) from 36 s to 35.9 min of memory. Baselines show high recall but low SR, so the missing ingredient is task detail (3D box centers, keyframes), not retrieval coverage. There are no formal ablations.
method: OmniMem: three databases built without knowing the query: NVILA captions per M-second clip in Milvus (text embedding, timestamp, pose), OpenGraph-style 3D primitives (RAM + Grounding-DINO + TAP, 4DMOS dynamic filtering, DBSCAN), and annotated keyframes at about 1 Hz with primitive-index contour labels.
Caption-induced primitive subset: query Milvus with task keywords, keep captions above a normalized similarity threshold tau, and take the union of their primitive indices as the working set X'_Q.

Task-conditioned IB clustering: start from singleton clusters on X'_Q, greedily merge neighbouring clusters with the smallest d_ij = (p_i+p_j)·JS(p(y|x_i),p(y|x_j)), and stop when fractional information loss exceeds a threshold. p(y|x) comes from cosine similarity to task cues, with a null-task floor alpha and top-k truncation.

Cluster-wise grouping and selection: assign each retrieved caption to clusters whose primitives overlap its indices, take the highest-scoring caption per cluster, rank representatives by query similarity and keep the top-K as R_text.
Keyframe selection: the LLM picks keyframe timestamps from R_text and loads those images from the keyframe DB, giving multimodal evidence R = R_text ⊕ R_img.

Agentic RAG workflow: an MLLM planner (GPT-4.1-mini) does up to three tool-call rounds, calling text, time and position query APIs. It answers with a 3D bounding-box center for spatial queries or a time-ago value for temporal ones, and the location is sent to Nav2.

setting.backbone: GPT-4.1-mini (frozen) for planner and answer generation; NVILA (NVILA-Lite-2B quantized on robot) for captions; RAM/Grounding-DINO/TAP for perception
setting.observation: RGB + depth or LiDAR with poses (Cartographer SLAM), sampled at 10 Hz; text or text+image queries
setting.action_space: Outputs a goal pose (3D location) or answer; navigation executed by ROS 2 Nav2 on a pre-built map
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (WH-VQA); NaVQA is offline CODa data; real Husky robot
setting.privileged: Assumes pre-explored environment with memory built by teleoperation (deliberate revisits); poses from SLAM/dataset; no other GT

numbers.eval_set_note: 188 of 210 queries (22 outside the memory window excluded); short memory (<2 min)
numbers.extra: pre-built memory; success if L2 error <15 m
100 tasks in Isaac Sim warehouse; success if L2 error <5 m

numbers_note: Overall correctness on NaVQA appears only in Fig. 3(a) and is not given as numbers. Temporal short/medium and text short/medium results are in Table 1 but were not all copied here. NaVQA has no official split names, so 'test' is used.
results: STaR beats ReMEmbR and OpenGraph on NaVQA and WH-VQA, especially at long horizons. On long-memory spatial questions SR is 0.77 vs 0.49 (ReMEmbR) and 0.26 (OpenGraph), and error is 16.9 vs 53.9 m. On WH-VQA spatial SR is 0.67 vs 0.39 (ReMEmbR), with error 6.5 vs 12.6 m. Average query time is stable at about 30.1 s across memory lengths.
limitations: Requires a pre-explored environment with memory built beforehand; not usable in unexplored settings.
Only two baselines, with no component ablations. WH-VQA is small (100 tasks) and self-built, and query latency is about 30 s, dominated by answer generation.
Keyframe storage grows large (4.3 GB for 35.9 min), and the task cues are chosen by an LLM planner.
